title: Angles & the Pythagorean Theorem
description: WASSCE-style questions on angle facts, parallel lines, polygons, bearings, and Pythagorean applications.

questions.q: Two parallel lines are cut by a transversal. If an angle corresponding to $x$ is $118^\circ$, find $x$.
questions.explanation: When parallel lines are cut by a transversal, corresponding angles are equal. Therefore $x=118^\circ$.

questions.q: The two remote interior angles of a triangle are $42^\circ$ and $68^\circ$. Find the exterior angle $x$.
questions.explanation: An exterior angle of a triangle equals the sum of the two remote interior angles: $42^\circ+68^\circ=110^\circ$.

questions.q: The right-triangle diagram models a ladder against a wall. The ladder is $13$ m and the wall height is $12$ m. Find the distance of the foot of the ladder from the wall.
In an isosceles triangle, the vertex angle is $44^\circ$. Find each base angle $x$.
questions.explanation: The base angles are equal. Their sum is $180^\circ-44^\circ=136^\circ$, so each base angle is $68^\circ$.

questions.q: The exterior angle of a regular polygon is $45^\circ$. How many sides has the polygon?
questions.explanation: For a regular polygon, each exterior angle is $360^\circ/n$. Thus $n=360/45=8$.

questions.q: A rectangle has length $15$ cm and width $8$ cm. Use the diagonal idea to find the diagonal $d$.
questions.explanation: The diagonal is the hypotenuse of a right triangle: $d^2=15^2+8^2=225+64=289$, so $d=17$ cm.

questions.q: A line from $A$ to $B$ makes a clockwise angle of $68^\circ$ from north. Write the bearing of $B$ from $A$.
questions.explanation: Bearings are measured clockwise from north and written with three digits. Therefore the bearing is $068^\circ$.

questions.q: A student walks $9$ km east and then $12$ km north. Use the right-triangle route idea to find the direct distance from the starting point.
questions.explanation: The route forms a right triangle. $d=\sqrt{9^2+12^2}=\sqrt{225}=15$ km.

questions.q: A tangent touches a circle at $T$, and $OT$ is a radius to the point of contact. Find the angle between $OT$ and the tangent.
questions.explanation: A radius drawn to the point of contact of a tangent is perpendicular to the tangent. Therefore $x=90^\circ$.

questions.q: Two right triangles are similar. The smaller triangle has corresponding sides $6$ and $8$; the larger triangle has the side corresponding to $6$ equal to $15$. Find the side corresponding to $8$.
questions.explanation: The scale factor from the small to large triangle is $15/6=2.5$. The side corresponding to $8$ is $8\times2.5=20$.

questions.q: Two adjacent angles on a straight line are $(3x+20)^\circ$ and $(2x-10)^\circ$. Find $x$.
questions.explanation: Angles on a straight line add to $180^\circ$: $(3x+20)+(2x-10)=180$. Thus $5x+10=180$, so $x=34^\circ$.

questions.q: A rhombus has diagonals $10$ cm and $24$ cm. Use the diagonal property to find its side length.
questions.explanation: The diagonals of a rhombus bisect each other at right angles. Half the diagonals are $5$ cm and $12$ cm, so $x=\sqrt{5^2+12^2}=13$ cm.

questions.q: Two parallel lines are cut by a transversal. Co-interior angles are $(2x+15)^\circ$ and $(3x-5)^\circ$. Find $x$.
questions.explanation: Co-interior angles on parallel lines sum to $180^\circ$. So $2x+15+3x-5=180$, giving $5x=170$ and $x=34$.

questions.q: The angles of a triangle are $45^\circ$, $(2x+5)^\circ$, and $(3x-20)^\circ$. Find $x$.
questions.explanation: Angles in a triangle sum to $180^\circ$. So $45+2x+5+3x-20=180$, giving $5x+30=180$, so $x=30$.

questions.q: A regular polygon has each interior angle equal to $150^\circ$. How many sides has it?
questions.explanation: Each exterior angle is $180^\circ-150^\circ=30^\circ$. Number of sides is $360/30=12$.

questions.q: A rectangle has diagonal $25$ cm and width $7$ cm. Find its length.
questions.explanation: Let the length be $l$. Then $l^2+7^2=25^2$, so $l^2=625-49=576$ and $l=24$ cm.

questions.q: A man walks $6$ km north and then $8$ km east. Find his bearing from the starting point, correct to the nearest degree.
questions.explanation: The bearing angle from north satisfies $\tan\theta=8/6$. Thus $\theta\approx53^\circ$, so the bearing is $053^\circ$.

questions.q: The exterior angle of a triangle is $126^\circ$. One opposite interior angle is $48^\circ$. Find the other opposite interior angle.
questions.explanation: An exterior angle equals the sum of the two opposite interior angles. The missing angle is $126^\circ-48^\circ=78^\circ$.

questions.q: A chord is $24$ cm long and is $5$ cm from the centre of a circle. Find the radius of the circle.
questions.explanation: The perpendicular from the centre bisects the chord, so half the chord is $12$ cm. Radius $=\sqrt{12^2+5^2}=13$ cm.

questions.q: The bearing of $B$ from $A$ is $070^\circ$. Find the bearing of $A$ from $B$.
questions.explanation: Reverse bearings differ by $180^\circ$. $070^\circ+180^\circ=250^\circ$.

questions.q: Find $x$ if $2x+40^\circ=180^\circ$.
The exterior angle of a triangle equals:
options: sum of the two opposite interior angles
sum of all three interior angles
questions.explanation: An exterior angle equals the sum of the two remote interior angles.

questions.q: A triangle has sides $7,24,25$. What type is it?
Find the diagonal of a rectangle $9$ cm by $12$ cm.
If an angle is $x$ and its vertically opposite angle is $78^\circ$, find $x$.
questions.explanation: Vertically opposite angles are equal.

questions.q: A triangle has angles $x,2x,3x$. Find $x$.
Which angle is obtuse?
questions.explanation: An obtuse angle is greater than $90^\circ$ and less than $180^\circ$.

questions.q: Which angle is reflex?
questions.explanation: A reflex angle is greater than $180^\circ$ and less than $360^\circ$.

questions.q: Find the length of the hypotenuse when the legs are $9$ and $40$.
Find the missing leg if the hypotenuse is $10$ and one leg is $8$.
A rhombus has perpendicular diagonals $6$ cm and $8$ cm. Find the side length.
questions.explanation: Half-diagonals are $3$ and $4$, so the side is $\sqrt{3^2+4^2}=5$ cm.

questions.q: The angle sum of a quadrilateral is:
questions.explanation: A quadrilateral can be split into two triangles, so its angle sum is $360^\circ$.

questions.q: Find one angle of a regular hexagon.
questions.explanation: Interior angle of a regular $n$-gon is $(n-2)180/n$. For $6$, it is $120^\circ$.

questions.q: The exterior angle of a regular pentagon is:
questions.explanation: Each exterior angle is $360/5=72^\circ$.

questions.q: If a bearing is $090^\circ$, the direction is:
questions.explanation: A bearing of $090^\circ$ points due East.

questions.q: If $a^2+b^2<c^2$ for the longest side $c$, the triangle is:
questions.explanation: When the square of the longest side is greater than the sum of the other squares, the triangle is obtuse.

questions.q: Find the distance between $(0,0)$ and $(6,8)$.
questions.explanation: Use Pythagoras: $\sqrt{6^2+8^2}=10$.

questions.q: A pole casts a shadow $5$ m long. The top of the pole is $13$ m from the tip of the shadow. Find the pole height.
If two angles are supplementary and one is $4$ times the other, find the smaller angle.
questions.explanation: Let the smaller angle be $x$. Then $x+4x=180$, so $x=36^\circ$.

questions.q: The longest side of a right triangle is called the:
questions.explanation: The side opposite the right angle is the hypotenuse.
